title: Skin-Inspired Electronics: An Emerging Sensing and Computing Platform
problem: Current tactile sensing systems lack the dense sensor integration and neuromorphic encoding needed to replicate skin's rich mechanoreceptive capabilities for prosthetic feedback and wearable/implantable applications.
motivation: Prosthetic limbs and wearable devices require seamless sensory feedback (shape, texture, temperature, pain) to enable natural dexterity and user interaction without relying solely on visual cues.
method: The platform uses densely packed tactile sensors (many touch sensors positioned close together) to capture fine-grained pressure and touch patterns. These sensor signals are processed by neuromorphic encoding circuits—circuits that work like the brain's nervous system, converting raw sensor data into neural-like signals. A neuromodulator component adjusts these signals in real time based on feedback. Since sensing and signal processing both happen together in one integrated system, it can be embedded directly into prosthetics, wearables, or implanted devices without needing external computation.
key_novelty: The key innovation combines dense touch sensors with neuromorphic encoding (brain-mimicking signal processing) and integrated neuromodulation to enable prosthetics and wearables to locally sense and interpret tactile feedback.
contributions: Highly dense tactile sensor array architecture
Neuromorphic signal encoding matching peripheral nervous system processing
Platform design enabling prosthetic, wearable, and implantable applications
primary_theme: neuromorphic tactile sensing for prosthetics and wearables
